does: Builds a sauce from a flavouring base cooked in fat, a liquid and a short simmer, until it coats a spoon. It is seasoned at the end, and strained or blended if it should be smooth.

intro.what: This sauce method combines a flavouring base cooked in fat with gradually added liquid.
intro.why: It teaches you to build smoothness and spoon-coating body before making the final seasoning adjustment.

how: Cook the flavouring base in the fat first: a roux, tomato, or a spice such as paprika stirred into oil off the heat.
Add the liquid a little at a time, whisking, until the sauce is smooth.
Simmer gently, stirring now and then, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Blend or strain it if it should be smooth.
Taste and season last, because a sauce grows saltier as it thickens.

cues.text: It coats the back of a spoon, and a finger drawn through the coat leaves a clear line.
Round and clean, with neither a raw floury taste nor a raw sharpness of spice.

mistakes.mistake: Salting early and then boiling the sauce down, so that it ends up too salty.
Pouring all the liquid in at once, which makes lumps.
mistakes.fix: Add it a little at a time and whisk.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring a spice into hot oil, where it burns and turns the sauce bitter.
mistakes.fix: Take the pan off the heat first.

quiz.question: Why judge final seasoning after this sauce has simmered down?
choices: Reduction can make the salt already present taste stronger.
Early salt stops the sauce thickening as liquid leaves.
Early salt prevents lumps when the liquid meets the base.
quiz.because: Concentration can make early seasoning too salty, so judge the sauce after thickening.

quiz.question: How do you join the liquid to the cooked base?
choices: Pour it all in before starting to mix.
Add the liquid only after the base has finished simmering.
quiz.because: Gradual additions and whisking help prevent lumps as the sauce comes together.

quiz.question: What spoon cue indicates the intended body?
choices: A bare spoon without a coating.
Large dry lumps clinging to the spoon.
A coating that holds a clear line drawn through it.
quiz.because: A spoon coating with a clear line shows a smooth thickened sauce.

quiz.question: Paprika scorched when added to hot oil. What would you change next time?
choices: Take the pan off the heat before stirring it in.
Leave the oil on high heat for longer.
Add the paprika before heating the empty pan.
quiz.because: Moving the pan off the heat avoids burning the delicate spice into bitterness.

comes_after.why: A sauce is brought to its body at a simmer.
